title: Field Service Analytics Software for Service Heads
meta: Field service analytics from the work itself: call volume and ageing, repeat visits, engineer load, spares consumed, SLA breaches and contract profitability.
h1: The service numbers that tell you where the week went.
pill: For service heads reviewing the month
sub: Aura Business reports on the service operation from the records the desk and the engineers already create: how many calls came in, how long they stayed open, who closed them, what spares they consumed and which contracts are worth keeping.

persona: Service head or operations director reviewing a field service operation month by month

sections.h2: Analytics that come out of the work, not out of a form
paras: Service reporting fails in most companies for one reason: the numbers are compiled separately from the work. Someone asks the desk for a call count, the desk types a sheet, and by the time it is ready it describes a month that has already gone.

In Aura Business the reporting is a by-product. The call was logged at intake, the engineer was dispatched from the desk, the job card was closed on the phone with spares recorded, the SLA timer ran on its own, and the invoice came from the closed job. Every figure a service head wants is already in those records.

What follows is the set of questions a service operation should be able to answer at any moment, and where each answer comes from. Nothing here is a benchmark or an industry claim; the figures are yours, drawn from your own calls.

sections.h2: Six things a service head is usually asked and cannot prove.
sections.lead: Not knowing is manageable. Not being able to find out is what makes the month a guess.

items.h: How many calls are open right now
items.p: The desk counts by scrolling a chat history, and the count changes depending on who does it.

items.h: How old is the oldest one
items.p: A call that has been open for three weeks is invisible until the customer escalates it.

items.h: Are we fixing things on the first visit
items.p: Repeat visits to the same asset for the same fault are never counted, so the pattern is never noticed.

items.h: Is the team busy or overloaded
items.p: Jobs per engineer per day is not recorded, so headcount decisions are made on the loudest complaint.
Parts leave stock without being booked to a job, so consumption cannot be traced to work done.
Contract revenue is known, the cost of serving each contract is not, so renewals are priced on last year's figure.

sections.h2: From one service call to the month's picture.

steps.p: Customer, asset, fault and contract status captured when the call is logged, with the SLA clock started.
Assignment by skill and area gives every job a named owner and a time it was allocated.

steps.h: The job card records the work
steps.p: Fault found, work done, spares consumed and the customer's signature, captured on site.
Resolution time and any SLA breach are recorded against the call without anyone calculating them.
Spares drop from inventory against the job, and chargeable work becomes a service invoice.
Volume, ageing, utilisation, consumption and contract performance are read from those same records.

items.q: Do you report a first-time fix rate?
items.a: The platform records every visit against the asset, so repeat visits for the same fault are visible in service history and can be reviewed. Treat it as a pattern you can inspect rather than a single headline figure.

items.q: Where does engineer utilisation come from?
items.a: From jobs assigned and closed per engineer over a period, alongside route and roster load and attendance. It describes how work is distributed, not how hard anyone worked.

items.q: Can we see which contracts lose money?
items.a: Calls, visits and spares are booked against the contract, so the cost of serving it can be read next to what it bills. See contract management.

items.q: Is there a report builder, or fixed dashboards?
items.a: Both. The owner dashboard gives the standing service views, and the reports engine produces cuts by customer, engineer, asset, product line or territory. Specific report layouts are agreed during setup.

items.q: Do engineers have to fill in anything extra for this?
items.a: No. Everything comes from the job card they already complete on the phone and from the desk's dispatch record. No separate reporting form is introduced.
Yes. Reports can be exported for board packs or for your accountant, and billing data can be exported to the accounting package. See Tally export.
